## **Costco Earnings Preview And Guidance**


**Next report focus: Q1 fiscal 2027**


Priority Factor To Watch Consensus Or Relevant Baseline What Matters At The Next Report


1 Revenue and underlying comparable sales Revenue consensus: **$74,243M** ; prior-year reported revenue: **$67,307M** Separate merchandise demand from gasoline inflation, foreign exchange and calendar effects. September comparable sales excluding all gasoline sales and FX were + **7.5%** .


2 EPS and tariff-refund accounting EPS consensus: $4.91; prior-year reported EPS: $4.50 Identify the net contribution from tariff refunds after reinvestment. The prior-year quarter also included a $0.16-per-share stock-compensation tax benefit.


3 Membership fee income and membership quality Latest paid-member growth: + **3.8%** ; Executive Membership growth: + **9.4%** Assess whether Executive upgrades, improving renewals and higher spending per member offset slower headline membership growth.


4 Gross margin and SG&A leverage Gross-margin consensus: **11.30%** ; prior-year reported gross margin: **11.32%** Distinguish underlying merchandise margins and productivity from gasoline mix, LIFO, tariff refunds and price reinvestment.


5 Digital and pharmacy growth September digitally-enabled sales: + **19.1%** excluding FX Look for incremental demand from expanded delivery partnerships, personalization and AI search, alongside pharmacy pricing headwinds.


6 Warehouse expansion and capital returns No company revenue, EPS or EBITDA guidance Update opening execution, capital-investment plans and special-dividend discussions; no special-dividend plan was disclosed at the latest report.


## **Summary And Conclusions**


- **Consensus requires double-digit revenue growth but slower EPS growth:** Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue implies **+10.3% YoY** , versus + **9.1%** implied EPS growth. Management does not provide numerical revenue, EPS or EBITDA guidance.
- **The prior-year comparison is meaningful, particularly in digital and membership fees.** Q1 fiscal 2026 delivered + **8.2%** net-sales growth, + **20.5%** digitally-enabled comparable sales and + **14%** membership fee income. Reported EPS included a stock-compensation tax benefit.
- **The latest available intra-quarter operating update supports healthy underlying demand.** September comparable sales excluding all gasoline sales and FX were + **7.5%** , with worldwide traffic + **4.7%** . However, the Labor Day shift benefited September comparable sales by a little more than **50 bps** .
- **Reported EPS will require a refund bridge.** Management had already received a similar amount of tariff refunds early in Q1 fiscal 2027 as in Q4 and intends to reinvest the majority in member value. The net earnings contribution was not guided.
- **Membership quality is the principal operating debate:** slowing paid-member growth contrasts with record Executive penetration and improving renewal rates. Management expects recent membership growth rates to be more typical near term, rather than promising an immediate reacceleration.


The source documents do not provide the next earnings announcement date or October sales results. The consensus vendor labels Q1 fiscal 2027 with a November 30, 2026 period end; that date is not a company-confirmed quarter-end or reporting date.

### **September 2026 Forward Commentary**


- **Membership and renewals:** Management expects recent membership growth rates to be more typical of the near-term outlook. Higher Executive penetration should improve renewals over time; future Asian openings could lift headline membership growth. Greater Executive and gasoline engagement are expected to support incremental spending per member.
- **Tariff refunds:** Refund receipts and reinvestment will affect fiscal 2027 results. Management plans to disclose the net quarterly earnings impact. Q4 receipts of **$184M** represented a little more than one-third of expected total refunds, but no exact total or future EPS contribution was provided.
- **SG&A:** Management identified no new major impediment to leverage at the comparable-sales rate discussed by analysts. Healthcare and general-liability costs remain relevant pressure points; the employee agreement has moved into its second year.
- **Inflation and pricing:** Management did not provide a precise inflation forecast. Middle East developments and tariffs could materially affect the next 6 to 12 months. Cost savings, purchasing efficiencies, vendor collaboration and Kirkland Signature are intended to protect member value.
- **Digital and delivery:** Expanded Uber Eats and DoorDash access is expected to add incremental shopping occasions alongside Instacart. Integrating popular Costco Next brands and items into the main app and website is expected to improve the experience and increase sales. Management does not anticipate a fundamental change in warehouse design from younger, more digitally engaged members.
- **AI:** Better product data and pages are intended to make Costco’s all-in value more visible through large language models. Management sees opportunities for product sales and membership acquisition, with quality reviews expected to reinforce that positioning.
- **Healthcare:** The SCAN Health Systems partnership is intended to develop Medicare Advantage benefits offering greater member value. Convenience and pharmacy programs are expected to support momentum while mitigating drug-pricing headwinds.
- **Capital returns:** Management will evaluate special dividends with the Board but disclosed no plan. Achieving a yield similar to the last special dividend would require more cash because the share price is higher.
- **Merchandise:** Management expressed confidence in the holiday assortment and incoming quality goods. The churro was scheduled to return temporarily to all U.S. locations starting that month.


### **Earlier Forward Commentary**


Source Date Topic Forward Commentary


May 28, 2026 Tariff refunds Claims were expected to be submitted over the following few months, with approved refunds arriving on a rolling basis over the subsequent 2 to 3 months. The portion passed to members was intended to be returned in some form.


May 28, 2026 Membership and market share Management characterized **4%** to **5%** membership growth as more normal absent special events and expected further market-share growth from quality and value.


May 28, 2026 Gross margin and costs Margin components were expected to fluctuate by quarter. Mid-single-digit non-gasoline comps were associated with potential core operating leverage. Further nonfood inflation was anticipated as resin costs entered merchandise costs.


May 28, 2026 Retail media Management expected retail media to ramp as personalization scaled. It described **80%** to **90%** of generated value as reinvested in members. Google Commerce Media and YouTube collaboration was intended to simplify brand and agency participation.


May 28, 2026 AI and gasoline engagement AI search was viewed as a potential sales opportunity; more gasoline engagement was expected to strengthen long-term loyalty. No gasoline-price or sustained-volume forecast was supplied.


May 28, 2026 Delivery and capital allocation Management planned to evaluate delivery capabilities and possible further vertical integration. Growth investment remained the priority, including manufacturing capacity supporting Kirkland Signature; no special-dividend plan was disclosed.


March 5, 2026 Digital and productivity Future digital enhancements were expected to support faster digitally-enabled growth than overall sales. Automated pay stations were intended to enable approximately 8-second transaction times.


March 5, 2026 Advertising and AI Better personalization was expected to create additional advertising benefits, with most value reinvested in members. AI opportunities centered on member value and employee productivity.


March 5, 2026 Pharmacy Medicare drug-pricing changes were expected to have a small impact, not a material top-line headwind.


March 5, 2026 Merchandise and expansion Spring and summer assortment was expected to be more traditional, with confidence in fall planning. Canada expansion was supported over the next 5 years, and international expansion prospects were favorable from fiscal 2027 onward.


March 5, 2026 Capital returns Management favored growing the regular dividend, subject to Board approval, and considered special dividends an effective way to return excess cash; no special-dividend plan was disclosed.


December 11, 2025 Membership renewals Management aimed to close the digital-versus-warehouse renewal gap and reverse overall declines, while allowing for slight declines over the following quarters.


December 11, 2025 Digital and AI Digital sales were expected to outgrow overall sales longer term. Pharmacy pay-ahead and online cake and deli-tray ordering were on the app roadmap. Gas-business AI was expected to improve inventory management and incremental sales.


December 11, 2025 Retail media and personalization Personalization was intended to increase basket items and visits. Most retail-media value was intended for reinvestment in lower prices and member value.


December 11, 2025 Operating costs Mid-single-digit sales growth remained the approximate threshold for SG&A leverage. Management did not expect recurrence of the quarter’s 4-bps tax-assessment impact.


December 11, 2025 Warehouse strategy Future openings were expected to combine mature-market infill and new markets, supporting faster sales maturity in infill locations and greater sign-ups in new markets.


## **Report Checklist**


The central question is whether Costco can meet the revenue and earnings consensus while sustaining **non-gasoline demand, underlying fee-income growth and member spending** against a strong prior-year base.


The earnings bridge should separately identify tariff refunds and price reinvestment, stock-compensation tax benefits, LIFO, gasoline mix and underlying operating leverage. For the outlook, the most relevant updates are renewal improvement, Executive penetration, incremental delivery demand, pharmacy pricing mitigation and execution of the expanded warehouse pipeline.
